positions.title: Software Development Engineer
positions.description:
- Design and implement distributed software architectures in Java for handling large-scale IoT data throughput using Kinesis, S3, SQS, and DynamoDB
- Mitigate security vulnerabilities by refactoring outdated backend code and writing concise instructions explaining how to enable protection features for customers
- Handle bug reports from customers, promptly fix operational issues, and collect customer impact data; create team processes to prevent repeated mistakes
- Streamline team's code deployment and maintenance workflows by documenting standard operating procedures and development lifecycles

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
-Designed internal tool automating service request tasks, saving engineer’s time while responding to tickets triggered by operational service outages or customer issues
-Utilized AWS Lambda, SNS, and Step Functions to build system architecture and implemented the tool in Java as an extensible service that teams could configure for their own tickets

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
-Maintained 2 codebases utilizing React, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, and Jest for BuildingConnected, a web app for project bidding that construction contractors use
-Delivered customer-requested feature with Node and Express server-side routing for secure links that redirect to contractor's internal work qualification form

positions.title: Web Content Programmer
positions.description:
-Evaluate open-source textbooks in the Libretexts online wiki according to W3C accessibility standards
-Identify digital accessibility issues using SiteImprove's website checker
-Fix HTML source code, such as adding image alt-text and markup for data tables, to improve textbook usability for assistive technologies like screen readers

company.name: University of California, Davis - Student Disability Center

positions.title: Amazon Future Engineer SDE Intern
positions.description:
-Developed front-end web app for the AWS IoT web console using React with TypeScript, HTML, and CSS, which displayed IoT data collection schedules
-Collaborated with co-intern to design middleware API retrieving data collection schedules, and created data visualizations of these schedules using D3
-Enabled customers to understand how often data is collected, so they can modify data collection frequency and control their costs as needed
-Unit-tested code components using Jest testing framework to ensure code quality

positions.title: Team Leader
positions.description:
-Partnered with a co-Team Leader to supervise 18 campers, ages 6 to 8, during a summer camp 
-Rotated the campers through art, science, and physical exercise classes daily, collaborating with camp instructors to facilitate campers in completing classwork and projects
-Played games and social bonding activities with campers in order to welcome them and make them feel comfortable
-Resolved disputes between campers in a fair and understanding manner
-Ensured that campers were safe and accounted for by taking roll call throughout the day and checking that campers were picked up by registered guardians

positions.title: Teacher Assistant
positions.description:
-Tutored middle and high school students in a class of 25 for a Java programming course
-Explained programming concepts and answered students' questions to guide them through difficulties in classwork assignments
-Provided feedback to students when necessary on how to debug or improve code
-Graded students' homework and supervised them during tests

company.name: Academic Talent Development Program, UC Berkeley

positions.title: Staff Writer and Events Manager
positions.locationName: Mission San Jose High School, Fremont, CA, USA
positions.description:
-As staff writer, collaborated in teams of 2 to 5 students or worked individually to produce articles and investigative reports for 17 monthly newspaper issues over 2 school years
-Reached out to students, school faculty, and local government officials to conduct interviews
-As events manager, worked closely with a co-manager to organize 2 field trips, 2 fundraisers, a guest speaker event, and 4 social bonding events for the 46 students in the newspaper organization

honors.title: Regents Scholarship
honors.description: Merit-based financial award renewed every school year
honors.issuer: Issued by University of California, Davis · Sep 2017

volunteerExperiences.description:
-Worked with Professor Michael Neff at the UC Davis Motion Lab and conducted research on how dancers adjust their movements while reacting to changes in their choreography
-Learned to use a research software called DANCE which can parse motion-capture data and simulate character animation
-Added a C++ plugin to the software codebase that could align and compare character animations based on motion-capture data from recorded dance performances
-Designed a mural centered around the theme "Healthy Choices" and led a group of student artists in painting the mural across the wall of a school cafeteria

projects.title: Fall Detector iOS App - Swift
projects.description:
-Developed an iOS phone app with 3 other students at a hackathon that would detect whether the user had fallen, ask the user whether they were okay, and then automatically contact emergency services if needed
-Utilized Twilio API for sending text messages, analyzed accelerometer data from phone to detect a falling motion, and designed user interface of app using the Xcode IDE

projects.title: Interactive Game Show - Java
projects.description:
-Expanded upon old source code found online for a trivia game show modeled after the show "Who Wants to be a Millionaire," in which the user would win money for every question answered correctly
-Updated deprecated code and reorganized the different parts of the source program in order to make the code more readable
-Remodeled the graphical user interface, and added new parts such as an introductory start screen with game instructions, different trivia categories to choose from, and bonus features such as chances to skip hard questions
